record.classification: Retained dispatcher counter overflow for admitted CLI configuration; source witness only.
record.title: Represent dispatcher port exhaustion before advancing past the last port
record.contract_trace: The dispatcher admits any u16 base_port through Clap and stores next_port as Mutex<u16>. Each new request copies the port, then increments the retained counter before roster validation, scene provisioning or spawning. It later constructs SocketAddr(host,port) for the child CLI.
record.counterexample: With --base-port=65535, the first request evaluates u16::MAX+1 before launching. With overflow checks enabled this panics; with checks disabled it wraps the next port to zero. Even a request that later fails source admission consumes this advance. No process or socket was launched during this audit, and the active build overflow profile is not assumed.
record.repair: Give allocation an explicit available/exhausted state and advance with checked arithmetic. Preserve the final usable port as an allocation, then record exhaustion rather than panic or wrap to an implicit zero/ephemeral mode. Propagate a structured allocation failure to the owning request callback. Coordinate allocation timing with successful request admission and the actual child lifecycle; do not silently recycle a live port or invent a broad arbitrary maximum below the real socket range. Native u16 projection belongs at SocketAddr/CLI construction, not unchecked allocator state.
dependencies: F27 configured bind endpoint versus actual bound advertised endpoint
PC73 dispatcher claim/launch lifecycle and exact native receiving behavior; current source-complete fixes are not authorized
record.acceptance: The full supported u16 port range has an explicit last-allocation/exhausted policy; --base-port=65535 cannot overflow, panic or silently wrap to a different allocation mode. Failed scene or roster admission must not accidentally change the documented allocation policy. Preserve actual native SocketAddr serialization and claim-before-spawn authorization. No new tests or runtime checks.

record.classification: Retained configured-versus-bound endpoint disagreement for an ephemeral-port launch; source witness only.
record.title: Advertise the socket’s actual bound port when registering a tactical server
record.contract_trace: Args.addr is a SocketAddr used by setup_server to spawn AdventureSimulatorServer. on_server_started receives the native LocalAddr after the server binds and logs it, but create_tactical_server_for_request receives args.addr.to_string(). Native registration retains that configured string in TacticalServer.addr for clients. The actual native binding result is available but discarded as endpoint authority.
record.counterexample: For --addr=127.0.0.1:0, a socket uses an OS-selected port reported through LocalAddr. Registration instead publishes 127.0.0.1:0, so the retained endpoint is not the listening endpoint. The existing test Args fixture also uses port0, though its offline world-dump flow is not a claimed registration reproduction. Dispatcher wrap-to-zero(F26) is another conditional producer; this defect also exists independently for an explicit zero-port launch.
record.repair: Construct the advertised endpoint from the actual bound port. Keep configured listen address, bound native socket and any deliberately configured public host as distinct roles; do not blindly replace an explicit public host with an unspecified wildcard address. Carry the resolved endpoint through registration until actual SDK string encoding, instead of retaining configured port as a second authority. Reconcile dispatcher and server endpoint ownership once, preserving current explicit host policy and concrete bind/registration failures.
dependencies: F26 port allocation and PC73 dispatcher/claim/endpoint lifecycle
Actual client endpoint parser/connection and certificate handling remain connected inventory; do not infer TLS/cert policy from this string alone
record.acceptance: An explicit zero-port bind registers the actual listening port, and a fixed-port bind registers that same fixed port. Preserve the configured public-host contract, IPv4/IPv6 SocketAddr encoding and one-use server claim. No new tests or launch during discovery.
